headline: Committee advances land-fund disclosure bill, hears tax update

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The committee voted nine ayes to recommend passing Bill 81 on first reading and heard new TAT software goes live in October.
meeting.recap: The first item was Bill 81 (2025), which would require the County to disclose fund restrictions when it budgets money to develop County-owned land.[[0:11:17]] The administration said it had no objection to giving the extra information.[[0:12:40]] The budget director said the property was first bought as open space, but West Maui's need for affordable housing made it a possible housing site.[[0:35:22]] A motion was made to recommend passing the bill on first reading.[[0:50:02]] The motion carried with nine ayes.[[0:56:57]] The second item was an update on collecting the transient accommodation tax (TAT, a tax on short-term lodging), with no vote planned.[[0:57:38]] The finance deputy director said the new TAT software project is on schedule and a week ahead.[[0:58:20]] The new software is set to go live in October.[[1:25:11]] Finance said an all-counties meeting with the state Department of Taxation is planned for next month.[[1:32:20]]
meeting.next: The chair said the committee will see about sending a written question on chapter 91 compliance. A council member said an update on these projects will be held in HOU next month.

moments.q: "Yeah, that's what triggered it. So just one."
"So we have nine ayes, motion carries."

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: The County is studying a West Maui property bought as open space as a possible affordable housing site.
issues.why: The budget director said there is a significant need for affordable housing, particularly in West Maui.

deadlines.t: Update on the projects in HOU.

issues.next: A council member said an update on these projects will be held in HOU next month.
issues.brief: The housing department said the project is still in pre-development, with designs and infrastructure being planned.[[#1]] A council member said rents at some low-income housing projects are going up by $200.[[#2]] The same council member said a utility increase coming in October could be $50 to $100 instead of the usual $4 to $6.[[#3]]
